title: Table and column label metadata in the Iceberg REST catalog: moving the read path to a vote
summary: After a catalog community sync, Andrei Tserakhau restated the labels proposal as a single optional, read-only `labels` field on the load response holding flat key-value metadata the catalog already owns, with no interpretation or enforcement in the spec, and asked to move to a vote on the read path. Prashant Singh asked why the existing `config` map could not carry this and why a structured tag entity should not be defined first, citing inheritance, nested-field conflicts and stable identity for cross-catalog sync. Andrei answered that config is client configuration that can carry credentials, while labels are a separate scope, and that the read surface should precede the structured entity. Ryan Blue called reusing config dangerous and saw no reason to hold back a read-only field. Prashant said he would not veto. Andrei proposed adding guidance that clients treat labels as opaque unless they understand them. Kevin Liu supported the proposal.

positions.stance: Vote on a minimal read-only flat `labels` field now and handle structured tag entities, renames, identity and cross-system sync in a follow-up.

Questions the need for labels when `LoadTableResult` config already carries non-standard keys, and prefers defining the structured tag entity first because flat key-values lack inheritance and stable identity for governance and catalog sync.

Config is client configuration that clients merge into session and FileIO properties and that may hold secrets, so labels need their own field; the flat read path comes first and the structured entity is added later.
Mixing this metadata into catalog-controlled config is dangerous, and a read-only field should not wait on other endpoints, as with the function list and load endpoints.

Still prefers settling what tag metadata looks like (for example multi-valued labels) and consumption guidelines first, and is not convinced flat key-values suffice for governance, but will not veto a vote.
Proposes adding spec wording that clients should treat label contents as opaque unless they understand a label's semantics, while keeping the field minimal.
Supports the proposal and likes that use cases are left unspecified; wants implementations to keep interoperability in mind.

outcome.note: No vote result in this thread. The proposer intends to start a vote on the read path; the one stated objector said he would not veto.

why_it_matters: It records the arguments for a separate `labels` field instead of reusing `config`, and that the read path is headed to a vote ahead of any structured tag model.
